results.notes: The Figshare dataset corresponds to the extracted paper; all 57 shared columns agree exactly with the September Mendeley dataset after matching id_code. There are 360 unique id_code and id_prog values, one row per participant, and complete data for all three outcomes. No posted records or AI nonusers are excluded. Numbers originally randomized and any exclusions before deposition remain unknown. Treatment codes: T_AI, PR_AI, LOT_AI; control codes: T_NoAI, PR_NoAI, LOT_NoAI. Each participant has one composition. Average the four complete raw ratings grade_1 through grade_4 within id_code in the September data; the average equals Figshare grade_mean exactly for all 360 people. No rating is counted as a separate participant. Reproduced the AI coefficient and HC1 robust SE from Table 5 (PDF p. 23, printed p. 20): outcome on an intercept, AI, tournament, and piece_rate, with lottery omitted. Counts are checked against Table 5 and Table 2 (PDF p. 16). Computed difference instead uses the requested unadjusted treatment-minus-control arm means; it therefore need not equal the reproduced incentive-adjusted coefficient. Counts are compared exactly; means, SDs, coefficients, and printed SEs are compared at the printed three-decimal precision. Analysis uses float64 arithmetic and SD denominator n - 1. The session variable identifies 21 observed sessions, each containing only one of the six arms: four sessions per AI arm and three per no-AI arm. The paper mentions sessions conducted under the tournament condition (PDF p. 8) and common instructions read aloud (PDF p. 30), but does not explicitly document whether randomization assigned sessions or individuals. For uncertainty, sessions are treated as allocation clusters based on this evidence; this is an analysis assumption, not confirmation of the allocation protocol. Observed session sizes are 8 to 24, despite the paper saying up to 20. This contrast has 12 treatment and 9 control sessions; n_clusters counts the observed sessions in the contrast, not people. The SE is from participant-level OLS on an intercept and AI only, clustered by session, with the CR1 multiplier G/(G-1) * (N-1)/(N-2). It is independently checked using the squared session sums of arm-centered residuals divided by arm sample sizes squared. Means and SDs remain across participants, with equal participant weights. This clustered SE is distinct from the HC1 SE used solely to reproduce the paper. The design is between subjects with one writing task per person, so round=all and no first_round record applies. Combined-arm and same-incentive results share participants and are not independent samples.
